bugs.name: Blank Git migration destination name shows duplicate-name error before required-field validation
bugs.summary: Submitting the Git migration form with Repository name empty first shows a duplicate-name error and fills the field from the source URL; required-field validation appears only after clearing it and submitting again.
bugs.expected: Because the form marks Repository name as required, submitting while it is empty should block the migration and identify that field as needing input, rather than report a name conflict for a value the user did not enter.
bugs.actual: With the destination name visibly empty, the first submission displayed “The repository name is already used” and populated Repository name with the source repository name. After clearing it and submitting again, the browser blocked submission with “Please fill out this field.”
reproSteps: Sign in as momentic-admin and create a fresh initialized public repository.
Copy its HTTPS clone URL and open Create → New migration → Git.
Paste the clone URL and leave Repository name empty.
Click Migrate repository. Observe the duplicate-name error and destination name populated from the source URL.
Clear Repository name and submit again. Observe required-field validation.
bugs.reason: Human review rejected this claim as a product bug. Deriving the destination name from the source URL and reporting that this repository name already exists is acceptable behavior in this migration flow.
